body:
🔴 **Completed tool call re-emitted as duplicate raw text when a streaming reply hits the length limit** The leftover text after the length limit is computed as everything past the amount already emitted as content (`input_text.get(state.emitted_content_len..)` at `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2854-2858`) and re-sent as message content whenever it contains a tool-call marker, so any already-completed tool call sitting in that leftover is duplicated into the reply's text. Impact: When a GLM-4.7 streaming reply that already produced one or more tool calls stops at the max-length limit, those tool calls are repeated verbatim as raw text content, corrupting the response.
Why the byte-offset tail is not equivalent to the truncated block The input stream buffers raw model text per choice into `input_text` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2772-2785`), while `emitted_content_len` only counts bytes the jail actually emitted as `delta.content`. A completed `...` block is emitted by the jail as structured `tool_calls` (not content), so its raw text stays in `input_text` but is NOT counted in `emitted_content_len`. On `FinishReason::Length`, `dropped = input_text[emitted_content_len..]` therefore includes any completed tool-call blocks that preceded the truncation point, and the `dropped.contains("")` guard (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2859`) still fires, re-emitting them as content. Worse, when prose is emitted *after* a suppressed tool-call block, the byte offset no longer aligns to a semantic boundary (it points into the middle of the buffered raw text), producing a garbage slice (or an empty string on a non-UTF-8 boundary). The non-streaming aggregator avoids this by isolating only the last block with no matching `` via `rfind` (`lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs:400-408`), so completed tool calls are never re-emitted. The streaming `saw_tool_call` flag is computed (`preprocessor.rs:2844-2846`) but never used to gate recovery, and the comment at `preprocessor.rs:2847-2849` deliberately recovers regardless, which is what triggers the duplication.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Unconditional arguments normalization changes rendered prompt for all models, not just GLM-5.2** `normalize_tool_call_arguments` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor/prompt.rs:42-63`) is invoked from both `NvCreateChatCompletionRequest::messages()` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor/prompt.rs:71-72`) and `UnifiedRequest::messages()` (`lib/llm/src/protocols/unified.rs:466-467`) unconditionally for every model, not gated on GLM-5.2. It rewrites `tool_calls[*].function.arguments` from the OpenAI wire-format JSON string into a JSON object before MiniJinja rendering. Chat templates that render arguments as a raw string (e.g. `{{ tool_call.function.arguments }}` expecting the JSON string) will now receive a map and render differently (map Display vs the original string), which can change prompt tokens / break exact parity for non-GLM models in multi-turn conversations containing prior assistant tool_calls. Many HF templates instead expect an object with `| tojson`, so the change may be correct for those — but the blanket application across all models warrants verification against the model families in use. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Streaming truncation recovery is unsound for n>1 (multiple choices)** In `apply_tool_calling_jail`, `input_text_buf` concatenates `delta.content` across ALL choices in each chunk (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2746-2754`) and `output_content_len` sums content bytes across all choices (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2809-2814`). For requests with n>1 the interleaved per-choice content makes the `dropped = input_text[emitted..]` computation (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2829-2833`) meaningless, and the single `extra` recovery chunk is overwritten per choice and applies the same `dropped` text to every choice (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2844-2850`). Multi-choice tool calling is uncommon, but if it occurs the recovered content will be garbled. Consider keying the buffers/tracking per choice index. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

Recovery uses stream-wide input/output offsets and then writes the same recovered tail into every choice, which corrupts `n > 1` streams when different `choice.index` values interleave. Fix: track recovery state per `choice.index` and synthesize content only for the triggering choice.

<details><summary>🤖 AI Fix</summary>

In `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs`, inside `OpenAIPreprocessor::apply_tool_calling_jail`, replace the single `input_text_buf` and `output_content_len` with per-choice maps keyed by `ChatChoiceStream.index`, update them using each choice's index, and when length recovery triggers build the recovery chunk with only the recovered `ChatChoiceStream` for that index instead of iterating over all choices.

</details>

<!-- ai-fix: In `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs`, inside `OpenAIPreprocessor::apply_tool_calling_jail`, replace the single `input_text_buf` and `output_content_len` with per-choice maps keyed by `ChatChoiceStream.index`, update them using each choice's index, and when length recovery triggers build the recovery chunk with only the recovered `ChatChoiceStream` for that index instead of iterating over all choices. -->
Is there a smarter way to check this from template itself rather than based on model name?

This "<tool_call>" check probably isn't correct -- this is looking for a leaking tool call tag (ex: "<tool_call>"), but the tool call tag may be different across models. Not all models will emit a token that translates to the literal text "<tool_call>". This is probably specific to GLM in the context of this PR, but the code doesn't represent that.

✅ **Resolved**: The previous bug reported that the code only checked `choice.delta.tool_calls` on the finish chunk, missing tool calls emitted in earlier chunks. The current code now introduces a per-choice `ChoiceRecovery` struct with a `saw_tool_call` boolean that is tracked across the entire stream (lines 2815-2816: `state.saw_tool_call = true` whenever any non-empty tool_call delta is seen), and the recovery gate at line 2823 checks `!state.saw_tool_call`. This directly addresses the previous bug.

✅ **Resolved**: The previous analysis flagged that `normalize_tool_call_arguments` was applied unconditionally to all models. The current code now gates it behind `template_wants_arguments_as_dict(&self.inner.model)` (prompt.rs:79, unified.rs:467), which checks for 'glm' in the model name. The unconditional application concern is resolved. The current ANALYSIS_0001 raises a narrower, distinct concern about the 'glm' substring match being too broad.

✅ **Resolved**: The previous analysis flagged that streaming truncation recovery was unsound for n>1 because input_text_buf and output_content_len were shared across all choices. The current code now uses a per-choice `ChoiceRecovery` struct keyed by `choice.index` in a `HashMap<u32, ChoiceRecovery>` (lines 2735-2743), with per-choice `input_text`, `emitted_content_len`, and `saw_tool_call`. This directly resolves the n>1 concern.

🟡 **Recovering truncated tool calls can crash the response stream on non-ASCII text** The leftover text of a cut-off tool call is extracted by cutting the collected input at a byte position taken from a different (output) text (`state.input_text[state.emitted_content_len..]` at `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2826`), so if that position lands in the middle of a multi-byte character the whole streaming response crashes. Impact: A request that produces non-ASCII text before a truncated tool call could abort the entire response instead of returning the partial output.
Byte-offset slice across two independently accumulated strings `state.input_text` is accumulated from pre-jail `choice.delta.content` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2756-2757`) while `state.emitted_content_len` sums the byte lengths of post-jail emitted content (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2811-2813`). The slice `state.input_text[state.emitted_content_len..]` assumes the emitted content is a byte-exact prefix of the input. If the jail ever emits content that is not a byte-exact prefix (e.g. any normalization/trimming), `emitted_content_len` may not fall on a UTF-8 char boundary of `input_text`, and Rust string indexing panics. Using `input_text.get(emitted_content_len..)` avoids the panic by returning `None` on a non-boundary index.
```suggestion let dropped = if state.emitted_content_len < state.input_text.len() { state .input_text .get(state.emitted_content_len..) .map(|s| s.to_string()) .unwrap_or_default() } else { String::new() }; ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Arguments normalization could alter rendering for glm-5 templates that treat arguments as a string** `template_wants_arguments_as_dict` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor/prompt.rs:42-45`) matches any model name containing `glm-5`/`glm5` and then rewrites `tool_calls[*].function.arguments` from a JSON string to a parsed object before MiniJinja render. This is correct for GLM-5.2's `{% for k, v in _args.items() %}` template, but if any glm-5 variant's chat template renders `arguments` directly as a string (e.g. bare `{{ tc.function.arguments }}` without `tojson`), converting it to a dict would change the rendered output. The conversion also silently skips non-object JSON (arrays/scalars parse into a Value and get inserted, which would break `.items()` in the template), though the wire schema is expected to always be a JSON object. Gating is intentional per the PR description; flagging as a behavior-scope consideration for other glm-5 variants. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

✅ **Resolved**: The current code at lines 2830-2833 already uses `state.input_text.get(state.emitted_content_len..).unwrap_or("")` which is the defensive `.get()` approach that avoids panicking on non-char-boundary indices. The bug's concern is already addressed in the code.

✅ **Resolved**: The detection mechanism has completely changed from model-name-based gating (glm-5/glm5 substring) to template-source-based detection (detect_tool_arguments_mode scanning for .items() in Jinja source). The previous analysis about model-name matching and its risks is no longer applicable to the current code.

🟡 **GLM-5.2 argument fix never activates on the unified (Anthropic/Responses) request path** The unified request path normalizes tool-call arguments (`normalize_tool_call_arguments` at `lib/llm/src/protocols/unified.rs:471`) only when its argument mode is the parsed-object mode, but that mode is never assigned for unified requests, so the value stays at its default and the normalization silently never runs. Impact: Chat requests arriving through the Anthropic/Responses (unified) surface keep tool-call arguments as a raw JSON string, so GLM-5.2-style templates that iterate the arguments still break exactly as before the fix.
Why the mode is always default on the unified path The template-derived mode is only stamped onto the request object in the chat-completions operator (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:3459`, `request.tool_arguments_mode = self.tool_arguments_mode;`). That assignment operates on a `NvCreateChatCompletionRequest`. Nothing ever sets `tool_arguments_mode` on a `UnifiedRequest`'s inner request before rendering; the field therefore keeps its `#[serde(skip)]` default `ToolArgumentsMode::JsonString` (`lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions.rs:132-133`). Consequently the guard `self.inner.tool_arguments_mode == ParsedObject` at `unified.rs:468-470` is always false and `normalize_tool_call_arguments` never runs for unified requests. (In practice both HTTP handlers call `into_inner()` — `http/service/anthropic.rs:316` and `http/service/openai.rs:2383` — routing through the chat path, so the added `UnifiedRequest::messages()` normalization is effectively dead code and provides no coverage.)
Prompt for agents ``` The normalization added in UnifiedRequest::messages() (lib/llm/src/protocols/unified.rs:466-472) guards on self.inner.tool_arguments_mode == ParsedObject, but tool_arguments_mode is only ever written on the NvCreateChatCompletionRequest chat-completions path (lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:3459). For UnifiedRequest, the inner request's tool_arguments_mode is never populated from the template, so it stays at the default JsonString and this branch never executes. Determine whether UnifiedRequest::messages() is actually reached (both anthropic.rs and openai.rs currently call into_inner() first, which would make this dead code), and if the unified path is intended to be supported, ensure the template-derived mode is propagated onto the inner request before rendering (e.g. by stamping self.inner.tool_arguments_mode wherever the unified request is preprocessed, mirroring preprocessor.rs:3459). ```
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Streaming recovery depends on jail emitting content byte-identical to input** The streaming truncation-recovery logic computes the dropped text as `input_text.get(state.emitted_content_len..)` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2852-2856`). `input_text` accumulates the raw `choice.delta.content` bytes entering the jail (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2776-2782`), while `emitted_content_len` accumulates the byte length of `content` deltas the jail emits (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2841-2843`). This is only correct if the jail emits prose content that is a byte-exact prefix of the raw input content — i.e. the glm47 jail never rewrites/trims/collapses content it passes through, and only ever withholds a trailing `...` block. If the glm47 jail transforms any pass-through content (whitespace normalization, marker stripping, re-chunking that changes total bytes), the offset would misalign and `dropped` could duplicate already-emitted text or omit part of the truncated block. The `dynamo-parsers` crate is an external crates.io dependency (Cargo.toml:60) so this pass-through invariant could not be verified from the repo. Worth confirming against the glm47 jail implementation. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

✅ **Resolved**: Resolved: the code switched from a per-request field (self.inner.tool_arguments_mode) to a thread-local ToolArgumentsModeGuard set in the common preprocess_request_with_options path. The unified path's messages() now reads get_tool_arguments_mode_for_render() which correctly picks up the thread-local set by the preprocessor before apply_template. The mechanism the previous bug described no longer exists.

🟡 **Cut-off tool calls are kept in streamed replies but thrown away in non-streamed replies** The leftover partial tool-call text from a reply that got cut short is discarded (`choice.text = String::new()` at `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs:437`) for non-streamed replies, even though the streaming path keeps the same text and returns it to the caller, so the two reply modes disagree and non-streamed callers silently lose the text. Impact: A non-streaming client whose tool call is truncated at the token limit receives empty content, while a streaming client on the identical trajectory receives the partial text — defeating the token-parity goal for aggregated responses.
Opposite handling in the two recovery paths The streaming path added in `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2848-2870` computes the dropped text and emits it as a synthetic content delta (`rc.delta.content = Some(dropped.clone())`), explicitly preserving the raw `` markup as content for TRT-LLM parity. The non-streaming aggregation path in `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs:422-438` detects the exact same condition (`parser == "glm47"`, `finish_reason=Length`, text contains ``) but instead of returning the text as content, it clears it (`choice.text = String::new()`). Before this PR the aggregator left `choice.text` as the raw partial text, so this change actively removes content that used to be returned. The PR description states the non-streaming path is "also covered" to match TRT-LLM behavior, but it does the opposite of the streaming path.
Prompt for agents ``` The non-streaming aggregation path in ChatCompletionAggregator::from_annotated_stream (lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs around lines 422-438) handles a glm47 tool_call truncated at max_tokens by clearing choice.text to an empty string. This contradicts the streaming path in OpenAIPreprocessor::apply_tool_calling_jail (lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs around lines 2848-2870), which preserves the dropped partial text and emits it as content for TRT-LLM parity. Decide on a single consistent behavior across both paths: either both preserve the partial text as content (matching the PR's stated TRT-LLM parity goal and the streaming implementation) or both drop it. As written, streaming clients and non-streaming clients receive different results on identical truncated trajectories, and the non-streaming path also regresses prior behavior where the raw partial text was returned as content. ```
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

✅ **Resolved**: The previous bug claimed the aggregator clears choice.text with `String::new()` at line 437. In the current code, the glm47 branch only logs a warning and explicitly leaves choice.text unchanged (comment: 'choice.text already holds the raw text; leave it as content.'). The clearing behavior no longer exists, so the bug is resolved.

📝 **Info: saw_tool_call suppresses recovery for a later truncated tool call** In streaming recovery, `saw_tool_call` is a sticky per-choice flag (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2844-2846`). If a stream emits one complete tool call and then begins a second `` block that is truncated by `finish_reason=length`, the sticky flag prevents any content recovery of the second, truncated block. This is likely an acceptable edge case (multiple tool calls with the second truncated is rare), but it is a behavioral corner that differs from the single-tool-call case the fix targets. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

📝 **Info: Tool-argument normalization not applied on the speculative-prefill render path** The `ToolArgumentsModeGuard` that enables `normalize_tool_call_arguments` is only installed around `apply_template` inside `preprocess_request_with_options` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:876-878`). The separate `formatter.render(...)` call in `lib/llm/src/preprocessor/speculative_prefill.rs:155` runs with the thread-local at its default (`JsonString`), so GLM-5.2-style templates that call `.items()` on tool-call arguments would render with the un-normalized JSON-string arguments on the speculative-prefill path. This is a safe fallback (matches pre-PR behavior) rather than a regression, but it means the parity fix does not cover that path if speculative prefill is used with such templates. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Log warning about truncated tool calls prints a large run of blank spaces** The recovery warning text (`tracing::warn!` at `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2858-2862`) contains a long run of embedded spaces in the middle of the message, so the emitted log line reads with a big gap between "content" and "on length finish". Impact: Operators reading frontend logs for the truncated tool-call recovery event see a malformed, hard-to-grep warning line.
Accidental whitespace in the string literal The single-line string literal `"glm47 streaming: partial emitted as content on length finish (TRT-LLM parity; raw markup in content)"` embeds many literal spaces (likely an editor wrap artifact). Rust preserves them verbatim in the log output.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Aggregation warning about truncated tool calls prints a large run of blank spaces** The aggregation-path recovery warning text (`tracing::warn!` at `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs:434-437`) contains a long run of embedded spaces mid-message, so the emitted log line reads with a big gap between "content" and "(TRT-LLM parity...)". Impact: Operators reading logs for the non-streaming truncated tool-call event see a malformed, hard-to-grep warning line.
Accidental whitespace in the string literal The string literal embeds many literal spaces (likely an editor wrap artifact); Rust keeps them verbatim in the log output.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Streaming recovery relies on jail forwarding the finish_reason=Length chunk** The streaming recovery in `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2836-2881` only fires when the jail output contains a chunk with `finish_reason=Length` for a choice that never emitted a tool_call. If the external `dynamo-parsers` jail were to swallow the trailing finish chunk (rather than forward it) when it drops a truncated `` at EOF, the recovery branch would never run and the dropped text would still be lost. The jail lives in the external `dynamo-parsers` crate (not in this repo), so I could not verify that it always forwards the `finish_reason=Length` chunk in the truncation case. Worth confirming against the jail's behavior / tests. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

✅ **Resolved**: No longer accurate. The code now deliberately does NOT suppress recovery based on saw_tool_call (comment at lines 2847-2849 says 'Recover even when an earlier tool call was already parsed'). The concern about sticky suppression no longer applies to the current code.

🔍 **normalize_tool_call_arguments silently leaves non-JSON argument strings as strings** `normalize_tool_call_arguments` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor/prompt.rs:300-326`) only replaces `function.arguments` when the string parses as JSON via `serde_json::from_str`. If a tool call carries an empty or malformed arguments string, it is left as a string. When the template is in `ParsedObject` mode (e.g. GLM-5.2 calling `.items()`), a leftover string would cause a MiniJinja render error at template time rather than a normalized empty object. Consider defaulting unparseable/empty arguments to an empty object to avoid render failures. Low likelihood in practice since the wire schema normally stores a JSON-object string. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

✅ **Resolved**: Resolved. The streaming recovery code has been completely rewritten to use rfind('<tool_call>') instead of the emitted_content_len byte-offset approach. The concern about byte-exact prefix alignment no longer applies.

🔍 **Template detection misses chat_template stored as a JSON array of variants** `mdc_jinja_template_text`'s `read_embedded` only extracts `chat_template` when it is a JSON *string* (`v.as_str()` at `lib/llm/src/preprocessor/prompt.rs:118`). Some HF `tokenizer_config.json` / `chat_template.json` files store `chat_template` as an array of `{name, template}` objects (e.g. a `default` and a `tool_use` variant). For those models the function returns `None`, detection falls back to `ToolArgumentsMode::JsonString`, and `normalize_tool_call_arguments` is never applied — so a model that ships its `.items()` template only in array form would still break at render. This is a fail-safe default (no regression for existing models) but an incomplete detection surface if such a model is deployed. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Streaming recovery relies on glm47 jail never emitting the partial as content** The streaming recovery buffers all raw input content per choice (`choice_recovery_in` at `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2769-2782`) and, on `finish_reason=Length`, re-emits the last unclosed `...` tail as a synthetic content chunk (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs:2832-2881`). This is correct only if the glm47 jail truly drops the truncated block and never optimistically emits any prefix of `` as content before deciding it's a tool call. If the jail (in the external `dynamo-parsers` crate, not in this repo) ever forwards a partial opening marker as content prior to truncation, that prefix would be duplicated: once from the jail's own content output and once from this recovery tail. The premise matches the PR description ("drops the block silently"), but this depends on external jail internals that could not be verified from this repository. Worth confirming against the glm47 jail implementation / a streaming test with a mid-`` truncation. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

✅ **Resolved**: This bug was wrong. In Rust, a backslash at the end of a line inside a string literal causes the newline and all leading whitespace on the next line to be consumed. The string literal uses `\` continuation (e.g. `"...content \\\n     on length finish..."`), so the rendered string has no extra spaces. There is no whitespace bug.

✅ **Resolved**: Same as above — the Rust `\` line continuation in the string literal strips the newline and leading whitespace. The aggregator warning string renders correctly with no extra spaces. The bug was wrong.

✅ **Resolved**: Resolved. The current code's read_embedded function now handles the JSON array-of-variants layout (lines 124-133 in prompt.rs), concatenating all template strings from the array so .items() patterns are detectable in any variant.

✅ **Resolved**: Resolved. The current normalize_tool_call_arguments (lines 334-354) now handles non-object JSON and malformed JSON by substituting an empty object with a warning log, rather than silently leaving the string.

✅ **Resolved**: Resolved. The speculative prefill path now passes tool_arguments_mode explicitly into SpeculativePrefillRequest and normalizes in messages() (speculative_prefill.rs:63-66), so GLM-5.2 templates are correctly handled on this path.

🔍 **UnifiedRequest::messages() normalization may be dead on current paths** The normalization was added to `UnifiedRequest::messages()` (`lib/llm/src/protocols/unified.rs:466-471`) reading the thread-local `get_tool_arguments_mode_for_render()`. However, both current UnifiedRequest entry points convert to the inner chat request before preprocessing — `unified_request.into_inner()` in `lib/llm/src/http/service/openai.rs:2382` and `lib/llm/src/http/service/anthropic.rs:316` — so template rendering runs on `NvCreateChatCompletionRequest`, whose `messages()` already applies the same normalization. The thread-local guard (`ToolArgumentsModeGuard`) is set only inside `preprocess_request_with_options` (preprocessor.rs:873). Unless UnifiedRequest is rendered directly under a guard somewhere, this added branch is effectively a no-op today. It is harmless/defensive, but worth confirming it is actually exercised or is intended for a future direct-render path. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔍 **Template-source priority for mode detection must match the formatter's own template selection** `mdc_jinja_template_text` (`lib/llm/src/preprocessor/prompt.rs:106-159`) prioritizes `mdc.chat_template_file` over `mdc.prompt_formatter` when extracting the Jinja source for `detect_tool_arguments_mode`. This is a heuristic used only to pick `ToolArgumentsMode`. If `prompt_formatter_from_mdc` ever selects a *different* template than the one `mdc_jinja_template_text` extracts (e.g. both fields populated with divergent templates), the detected mode could disagree with the template actually rendered — either failing to normalize dict args (GLM `.items()` render panic) or normalizing when not needed. For the targeted GLM-5.2 layout (embedded template in tokenizer_config, `chat_template_file=None`) the fallback path reads the correct source, so the common case is fine. Worth confirming the two selection orders stay in sync. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*
